, eutectic [3], non-equiatomic
[4], precipitation strengthened [5], interstitial [6] HEAs, TRIP and

during SPS can be attributed to the generation of high-power current

in CrFeCoNi and

[15]. These HEAs based composites’ mechanical properties were almost
similar to those of a few advanced composites prepared by powder
metallurgical processing

paramount importance to establish the thermal stability of these HEAs to
ascertain two aspects i.e., phase transformation and the retention of
nanosized structure. The CrFeCoNi HEA has revealed the high resistance
to grain growth even at long duration of heat treatment at
9 0 0 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }
for
600 h [15]. Shivam et al. [18] synthesized AlCoCrFeMnNi HEA by
mechano-chemical process and illustrated that the powder sample was
thermally stable up to
5 0 0 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }
and afterwards encountered diffusional
transformation to form minor fraction of intermetallics along with the
parent phase at room temperature.

strong effect on the phase constitution and mechanical properties on
steels, Ni-based and Co-based superalloys [19]. The addition of carbon

[22], Ni CoCuFeCr V

mechanical properties at room and high temperatures. Raabe et al. [27]
studied the FeMnAl–C and FeMnAlSi–C high entropy steel having FCC
structure and exhibiting good tensile ductility with nominal strength
[27]. They explained the formation of different phases by varying the C
and Mn content in the non equiatomic FeMnAlSi–C high entropy steel.
The effect of C and Mn in the phase formation of FeMnAlSi–C high en
tropy steel was shown efrom multiphase to single phase FCC solid so
lution. Raabe and co-workers illustrated the formation of FCC structure

In the view of above, the present investigation envisages the prepa
ration of a non-equiatomic low-density Fe Mn Ni Al Si C high
entropy steel by MA and SPS possessing a multi-phase microstructure
consisting of mainly BCC and B2 phases that may have greater strength
with appreciable amount of ductility. The alloying behavior, thermal
stability, microstructural and chemical analysis, mechanical properties
(i.e., microhardness and compressive strength) during MA and SPS have
been studied systematically. Further, the mechanical properties of these
HES were understood with the help of various strengthening
mechanisms.
2. Experimental details
The starting elemental powder of Fe, Ni, Mn, Al, Si and C (99.2%
pure) was taken in appropriate proportion of
0.25%; wt. %) and was milled in planetary ball mill (Model no. PM 400/
2, Retsch) at the speed of 200 rpm. The ball to powder ratio was taken as
10:1. The milling was carried out in the tungsten carbide (WC) vials and
with WC balls. To avoid oxidation, toluene was taken as a process
control reagent during milling. To understand the phase evolution
during milling, 2–3 g of milled powder was taken after every 5 h of
milling. The milling was stopped intermittently for 20 min after every 1
h for avoiding any overheating. The 35 h milled powder was consoli
dated by spark plasma sintering (Model no. Dr. Sinter SCM 1050, Japan)
at a temperature of
{ 9 0 0 } ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C } ,
pressure of 50 MPa, and heating rate of 100
^ \circ \mathrm { C } .
min<sup>−</sup> <sup>1</sup> with a holding time of 15 min. The diameter and thickness of
the spark plasma sintered sample (SPSed) was ~30 mm and ~9 mm,
respectively. The pellet was cleaned with the help of polisher to remove
the graphite layer. The wire EDM machine (Medha enterprises, model
no. EXPRESSCUT EX-2530) was used to cut the pellet into many pieces
of dimensions (diameter = 4 mm and
\mathrm { h e i g h t } = 8
mm) for further
characterization and evaluation of mechanical properties. The consoli
dated pellet was found to have a relative density of ~99%, which was
calcualted using the following [28]:
\rho_ {\mathrm{RD}} = \frac {\rho_ {\mathrm{exp}}}{\rho_ {\mathrm{th}}} \times 1 0 0\tag{1}
where,
\rho _ { \mathrm { R D } }

( \% ) , \rho _ { \mathrm { t h } }
is therotecial density computed by
the rule of mixture (6.55 g/cc), and
\rho _ { \mathrm { e x p } }
is experimental density calcu
lated by the Archmides principle [29]. The experiment was repeated six
times to calculate the average experimental density
( 6 . 4 9 \pm 0 . 3 \mathrm { g / c c } )
The differential scanning calorimeter (DSC) (Netzsch, DSC404
Pegasus) was used to study the thermal stability of milled powder. The

and
8 0 0 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C } )

milled powder at different milling time was examined using Evo 18 Carl
Zeiss scanning electron microscope (SEM), and field emission scanning
electron microscopee (FE-SEM) (FEI model no. Nova Nano SEM 450),
both equipped with EDS detector. The microstructural study of the
SPSed pellet was done with the help of FE-SEM (model no. Nova Nano
SEM 450). The elemental analysis of the SPSed sample was performed by
the EDS detector attached with SEM. For microstructural features, the
SPSed samples were systematically polished and chemically etched with

parameters and Thermo-Calc were correlated with the experimental

also shown. The ferritic dual phase steel has the microhardness in the

cate a low-density high entropy steel possessing good microstructural
stability as well as excellent mechanical properties having synergy with
ductility. In spite of having excellent microstructural stability and me
chanical properties, these SPSed HES were found to have a limited
ductility of ~19%. Further, efforts towards tailoring the composition for
designing and developing a low-density HES having excellent room
